title: Simultaneous normalized quotient/Roos models for primitive completed operations
statement: Fix a prime l, a finite extension E of Q_l, an arbitrary family W of schemes with l invertible in every residue field, and independent site, coefficient and family universes. There exist Models l E W as specified in the completed-operation substitution interface: the full reduction/total-limit calculus, a canonical system RingedSiteDualityModel with the canonical adjunction-compatible isomorphisms between its closed tensor and the calculus tensor and between the integral calculus tensor and IntegralOnSlice.duality, completion with its unit equation, a normalized IntegralComparisonRoosModel at every scheme and an IntegralComparisonPullbackModel for every morphism using these same models. The actual calculus counit is invertible on every normalized system, and the coefficient unit, system tensor and whole-system pullback preserve IsNormalizedCoefficientSequence. This asserts primitive construction and normalization only: it does not assert expression comparison, substitution or structural transport laws.

proof.text: The actual counit is invertible by purNormalizedReconstruction. Normalization is invariant under a whole-system isomorphism by transition naturality and cancellation of the induced bijections on Hom sets. Apply the quotient-expression normalization theorem to the empty family and unit expression. For tensor, write both normalized inputs as reductions using the actual counit, use reductionTensor, and transport along the canonical closed-tensor comparison. For pullback, apply effective quotient model descent to the reduction of the total limit, then transport along pullback of the counit.

For every scheme morphism, form inverse image of this same whole reduction system; the quotient/Roos comparison gives IntegralComparisonPullbackModel, normalized on every simultaneous quotient presentation. old_proof.text: Identify the actual unit, tensor and pullback transition adjuncts using the normalized system operation models. The unit adjunct is scalar multiplication, tensor uses monoidal scalar extension followed by the input adjuncts, and pullback uses inverse scalar association followed by pullback of the input adjunct. Their cocycles follow from scalar association and the input cocycles, hence all three preserve normalization. Transport through the same normalized representative comparisons of the preceding steps.
